senses.gloss: इत mfn. ifc. gone
returned
obtained (cf. अनित, उद्-इत, &c.)
remembered, L.
इत॑ (अ॑म्), n. way, ŚBr.
इतान्त mfn. gone to the end, Śiś.
इता॑सु mfn. one whose animal spirits have departed, TS.
इ॑-तर mf(आ)n. (the neuter is अद् in classical Sanskṛt, but अम् [अद्, ŚBr.] in Ved. Pāṇ. vii, 1, 25, 26; comparative form of pronom. base 3. इ; cf. Lat. iterum; Hib. iter), the other (of two), another
pl. the rest
(with abl.) different from, RV.; AV.; ŚBr.; MBh.; R.; Mn.; Ragh.; Hit. &c.
low, vile, Kād.
expelled, rejected, L.

इ॑-तर इतर, इतर, the one — the other, this — that. (इतर connected antithetically with a preceding word often signifies the contrary idea, e.g. विजयाय इतराय वा [MBh.], to victory or defeat; so in Dvandva compounds, सुखेतरेषु [ŚvetUp.], in happiness and distress; it sometimes, however, forms a Tat-puruṣa compound with another word to express the one idea implied in the contrary of that word, e.g. दक्षिणेतर, the left hand.)
इ॑-तरा (आ), f. said to be a N. of the mother of Aitareya
इ॑-तरद् (अद्), ind. whereas, whilst, Subh.
इ-तर—जन॑ m. an ordinary man, Śārṅg.
इ-तर—जन॑ (आस्), m. pl. ‘other men’
a euphemistic name of certain beings who appear to be considered as spirits of darkness (Kuvera belongs to them), AV.; VS.; TS.; MaitrS.; GopBr.
इ-तर—जातीय mfn. ordinary, common-place.
इ-तर॑—तस् ind. otherwise than, different from
from or to another direction, KātyŚr.; ŚBr. &c.
(इतश्चेतरतश्च, hither and thither, R.)
इ॑-तर—त्र ind. elsewhere, BhP.
on the other hand, else, Yogas.
इ-तर॑—था ind. in another manner, in a contrary manner
perversely
on the other hand, else, ŚBr.; KātyŚr.; Śiś. &c.
इ-तर—पाणि m. the left hand, ĀśvGṛ. iv, 7, 13.
इतराङ्ग mfn. being a means to another, ancillary to another, Sāh. 266.
इतरेतर mfn. (occurring chiefly in oblique cases of sing. and in comp.; perhaps for इतरस्-इतर; cf. अन्योऽन्य, परस्-पर), one another, one with another, mutual, respective, several
इतरेतर n. or adv. mutually, &c., KātyŚr.; MBh.; Ragh. &c.
इतरेतर—काम्या f. respective or several fancies or inclinations
इतरेतर—प्रत्यय mfn. dependent on each other
इतरेतर—प्रत्यय-त्व n. mutual dependance, Bādar.
इतरेतर—योग m. mutual connexion or relation (of the simple members, as in a Dvandva compound), Siddh. i, p. 431.
इतरेतराश्रय mfn. taking refuge with or depending on each other, concerning mutually
इतरेतराश्रय m. a particular logical error, circular reasoning, Sarvad.
इतरेतरोपकृति-मत् mfn. helping each other, Śiś. ix, 33.
इतरे-द्युस् ind. on another or different day, Pāṇ. v, 3, 22.
इ-त॑स् ind. (fr. 3. इ with affix तस्, used like the abl. case of the pronoun इदम्), from hence, hence, here, (opposed to अमु-तस् and अमु-त्र), RV.; AV.; ŚBr.; Śak. &c.
from this point
from this world, in this world, ŚBr.; ChUp.; Prab. &c.
(इतस्, इतस्, here — there; इतश्चेतश्च, hence and thence, hither and thither, here and there, to and fro)
from this time, now, RV.; AV.; MBh. &c.
therefore, R.
इत॑-ऊति mfn. extending or reaching from hence
existing or lasting longer than the present time, future
one who has obtained help [Sāy.], RV.
इतः॑-प्रदान mfn. offering from hence i.e. from this world, TS.; ŚBr.
इतः—प्रदान (इतः॑-; also) n. oblation from hence, TS.
इतः—प्रभृति ind. from hence, MBh.
इतस्-ततस् ind. here and there, hither and thither, R.; Hit. &c.
